questions.q: You have an Accounts column with values like "101 Bank/Cash at Bank" — a number, then a name, separated by exactly one meaningful space. Which "Split at" option should you use?
options: Each occurrence of the delimiter
Right-most delimiter
It doesn't matter which you choose
Left-most delimiter
questions.explain: Left-most delimiter splits only at the first occurrence — correct when just the first separator matters, like separating a leading account number from the rest of the text.

questions.q: When would "Each occurrence of the delimiter" be the right choice?
options: When you want to split at the very last delimiter only
When a value has a consistent, repeating structure, like a date written 2026-09-07 split on every hyphen
It's identical to Left-most delimiter
When you only want to split at the very first delimiter
questions.explain: Splitting at every occurrence produces one new column per split — ideal for values with a fixed number of repeating separators, like a structured date.

questions.q: What's the key difference between Split Column and Extract?
options: They do the exact same thing
Extract only works on number columns; Split Column only works on text
Split Column can only be undone by Merge Columns
Split Column replaces the original column with the pieces; Extract creates a new column and leaves the original intact
questions.explain: Split Column breaks the original column apart and replaces it. Extract pulls out part of the text into a brand-new column, while the original column stays as it was.

questions.q: Where do Merge Columns and Extract live in the ribbon?
options: View tab
Home tab, in the Reduce Rows group
Add Column tab, in the From Text group
Transform tab, in the Any Column group
questions.explain: Both Merge Columns and Extract are in the From Text group on the Add Column ribbon tab, alongside Format and Parse.

questions.q: Under Split Column's Advanced options, what does setting "Split into" to Rows do, instead of Columns?
options: Splits a cell holding a list of values into one row per value, instead of one column per value
Only works with the Right-most delimiter option
Has no effect — Rows and Columns behave identically
Deletes the original rows
questions.explain: Splitting into rows is for cells that hold a list-like value (e.g., "Cash, Receivables, Inventory") that should become separate rows rather than separate columns.
